# DevLog — PCB Design Session

**Date:** 11 October 2026
**Hours Logged:** 3 hours
**Session Focus:** PCB Schematic Design, Pin Mapping Correction & Documentation

---

## 🎯 What I Did

Designed the complete schematic and PCB layout for NeuroFocus using EasyEDA.
Learned the tool from scratch, discovered and fixed a critical hardware bug,
and documented the final design.

---

## ⏱️ Time Breakdown

| Phase | Task | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Learning EasyEDA from scratch | 90 min |
| 2 | First draft schematic | 60 min |
| 3 | Discovering strapping pin issue | 45 min |
| 4 | Redesigning pin mapping | 90 min |
| 5 | Final schematic + PCB layout | 75 min |
| 6 | Testing & verifying connections | 45 min |
| 7 | GitHub documentation | 45 min |
| 8 | Hack Club submission prep | 30 min |
| **Total** | | **8 hours** |

---

## 🔴 Critical Bug Found & Fixed

My first schematic had the microSD card on **strapping pins** (GPIO 0, 2, 12, 15).
These pins control boot mode on the ESP32. With the SD card attached at boot,
the device would fail to start.

**Fix — moved SD to VSPI:**
- CS → GPIO 5
- SCK → GPIO 18
- MISO → GPIO 19
- MOSI → GPIO 23

**Also relocated all peripherals to safe pins:**

| Component | New Pin |
|---|---|
| LEDs | GPIO 32, 33, 25, 26 |
| Buttons | GPIO 13, 14, 27, 4 |
| START / BACK | GPIO 34, 35 (input-only) |
| RGB LED | GPIO 16, 17, 15 |
| I2C (OLED + RTC) | GPIO 21, 22 |
| Buzzer | GPIO 2 (100Ω) |

---

## 💡 Key Learnings

1. **Strapping pins are real.** ESP32 datasheet is essential reading.
2. **VSPI is the safe default for SD cards** on ESP32.
3. **I2C can share a bus** — OLED and RTC work together on GPIO 21/22.
4. **Input-only pins (34, 35) are perfect for buttons.**
5. **EasyEDA is not mobile-friendly** — next time, use desktop.
6. **Peer review caught a bug** that would have cost a full PCB re-spin.

---

## 🚧 Challenges & Solutions

| Challenge | Solution |
|---|---|
| EasyEDA overwhelming on mobile | Switched to EasyEDA Standard |
| Couldn't find ESP32 DevKit in LCSC | Used EasyEDA Library |
| SD card on strapping pins | Moved to VSPI |
| AI-generated images had wrong text | Hand-drew diagram + used EasyEDA |
| Buzzer resistor too high | Changed 1kΩ to 100Ω |

---

## 📦 Final Design Summary

- **MCU:** ESP32 DevKit V1
- **Display:** 1.3" OLED (I2C)
- **RTC:** DS3231 (I2C, shared bus)
- **Buttons:** 6 (4 task + START + BACK)
- **Indicators:** 4 white LEDs + 1 RGB LED
- **Audio:** Passive buzzer
- **Storage:** microSD (VSPI)
- **Power:** LiPo 3.7V 2000mAh + TP4056

---

1. Run ERC (Electrical Rules Check) in EasyEDA.

3. Assemble on breadboard.
4. Write firmware for Simple RT task.
5. Run 30-day attention study.

### 2026-10-11 – ## 🎨 Hardware Design Comparison & Rejection Reasons

**4h**

## 🎨 Hardware Design Comparison & Rejection Reasons

We evaluated 4 hardware designs before finalizing the PCB. Here is why the first three were rejected:

### Design 1 — Black 2×2 Grid
- Non-linear spatial mapping adds cognitive load.
- Low contrast (black on black) reduces LED visibility.
- Complex PCB routing.

### Design 2 — Black Curved Arc
- Curved layout makes button mapping less intuitive.
- Low contrast.
- Curved traces complicate PCB design.

### Design 3 — Black Angled / Staggered
- Asymmetrical layout causes mapping confusion.
- Low contrast.
- Diagonal traces increase noise and routing complexity.

### Design 4 — White Body + Dark Grey Top + Straight Line + Colored Buttons ✅
- **Straight line** for linear mapping (1→2→3→4).
- **High contrast** (white LEDs on dark grey) for instant stimulus detection.
- **Colored buttons** for visual discrimination.
- **White body** for eye comfort during 30-day study.
- **Horizontal PCB traces** for simple, low-noise routing.
- **Professional, finished look.**

**Conclusion:** Design 4 meets all scientific, ergonomic, and manufacturing requirements.
